readme.html:
Picky

Render it ten ways. Keep the one you love.

▶ Watch the 2-minute demo (MP4 download)

▶ Try the editor in your browser — a recorded LAST ORDER project: play takes, read prompts and lint, pick, rate and fake-render. No GPU needed.

Picky is an open-weights film studio for MiniMax H3, made of a ComfyUI custom node pack and a browser editor. It runs on your own GPU.

Iterating on a shot in plain ComfyUI leaves you with a folder of ComfyUI_00342_.mp4 files, and you have to guess which prompt and seed made each one. Picky keeps every attempt attached to its scene. You render many takes of the same shot, compare them side by side and keep the best one. Then you take the next step on that take: render it at final quality, extend it, enhance it, or cut it into the timeline. Every result stays linked to the prompt version and the take it came from.

Built for #OpenSourceHiggsfield, as an open alternative to Higgsfield's Cinema Studio.

What you get:

  • Storyboard prompts, not prompt soup. Each shot is a structured document with style, overview, timed beats, camera, dialogue, soundscape and music. It is composed into MiniMax's official H3 prompt format for you.
  • A prompt linter that knows H3. It catches the ways H3 misreads a well-formed prompt before you spend GPU time on them: overfull beats, cuts with no new information, wasted quality tokens, missing soundscape and so on.
  • A cast. Characters and locations are defined once, with reference pictures. You write @Mara in any prompt, and at render time it becomes the right <Subject N> with that member's current references. Renaming a cast member rewrites every mention.
  • Text, image and reference to video. Supports first and last frames, ref2v with up to six references, and a Krea 2 keyframe studio for generating stills.
  • Extends that keep the shot. A continuation runs on the shot's own graph plus Motion Context, so the framing, cast and checkpoint carry over.
  • Takes and lineage. Sweep seeds, compare candidates, keep a full history of every prompt version, and fold extension chains back into one clip.
  • Quality tiers. Use a fast low-resolution preview for checking adherence, turbo HD for drafts, and a 2-pass latent upscale for final renders. SeedVR2 can enhance a take afterwards.
  • An AI writer that can stay on your machine. Describe a scene in a sentence, or ask for a change ("make the second beat handheld"). The writer edits only the fields in scope and then repairs its draft against the linter. It runs on any local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM). Gemini is an optional alternative.
  • Agent-driven. An agent skill teaches a coding agent the prompt format and the render loop, so it can author, revise and render through the editor's HTTP API while its edits appear live in the open editor. It ships for Claude Code in .claude/skills/video-prompt, and in .agents/skills/video-prompt for Codex and other agents that read that folder.

Requirements

  • An NVIDIA GPU with 24 GB of VRAM (tested on an RTX 4090). 720p at about 10 seconds fits in 24 GB. See docs/MINIMAX_H3_VRAM_AND_CONTEXT_GUIDE.md for the full table.
  • A recent ComfyUI with built-in MiniMax H3 support. The portable Windows build with Python 3.12 is tested.
  • ffmpeg on your PATH, for export and clip assembly.
  • About 60 GB of disk space for the H3 models.

Install

1. Install the node pack

cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone <this repo> picky

The face-restoration features need a few extra Python packages, installed into ComfyUI's Python. The rest of the editor needs only the standard library.

python -m pip install -r picky/requirements-faces.txt

2. Install the companion node packs

Pack Needed for
ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-Contex-Loop Extends (Motion Context)
Comfyui_Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler 2-pass tiers (latent upscale)
ComfyUI-SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler Enhance (optional)
ComfyUI-FeiHou-Easy-H3 and ComfyUI-FeiHou-Toolbox Face refine (optional)

Plain text-, image- and reference-to-video renders need only ComfyUI's built-in H3 nodes.

3. Download the models

These are all open weights. Put each file in the ComfyUI models/ subfolder shown.

File Folder Source
minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors diffusion_models Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3
minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors diffusion_models Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 (ref2v)
qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors text_encoders Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3
minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors vae Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3
minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors vae Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3
minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_comfyui_bf16.safetensors loras lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo (preview and turbo tiers)
minimax_h3_latent_upscaler_3d_fp16.safetensors latent_upscale_models LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler (2-pass tiers)
krea2_turbo_fp8_scaled.safetensors diffusion_models Comfy-Org/Krea-2 (keyframe studio)
qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors text_encoders Comfy-Org/Krea-2 (keyframe studio)

The SeedVR2 pack downloads its own models on first use.

4. Optional: a local model for the AI writer

Install Ollama and pull a model that handles structured JSON well. A Qwen 3 or Gemma 3 model of 8B or more works, for example ollama pull qwen3:8b. Then create ComfyUI/user/video_prompter/settings.json, or edit it if it exists:

{
  "llm_url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1",
  "llm_model": "qwen3:8b"
}

Any OpenAI-compatible server works. LM Studio's default is http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1, and llama.cpp's llama-server defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1. If you leave out llm_model, the first model the server lists is used. You can set the same values with the VIDEO_PROMPTER_LLM_URL and VIDEO_PROMPTER_LLM_MODEL environment variables.

If you prefer Gemini, set gemini_key instead. When both are set, the local server is used. Without either, the editor works normally and the writer buttons are disabled.

Run GET /video_prompter/llm/status to see which file path the settings are read from, and which provider is in use.

5. Start

Restart ComfyUI, then open http://127.0.0.1:8188/video_prompter/.

Picky was called Video Prompter during development. That name still appears in the Python package, the URL routes, the settings folder and the VIDEO_PROMPTER_* environment variables, so existing projects keep working.

A first film in five minutes

  1. New project, then Add source.
  2. Write a sentence in the writer bar, for example "night market, a cook flips a wok of noodles into the air, slow push in, 8 seconds". Or fill in the Scene tab yourself.
  3. Fix anything the Findings panel flags in red.
  4. Render on the preview tier with three or four seeds. Double-click the source to compare the takes, then choose one.
  5. Re-render the chosen seed on turbo_hd or final. Trim it on the timeline, add the next shot, then Export.

Documentation

  • docs/REFERENCE.md: the full manual, covering the prompt model, projects, takes, profiles, export and enhancement.
  • docs/EDITOR_USAGE.md: editor navigation.
  • docs/MINIMAX_H3_VRAM_AND_CONTEXT_GUIDE.md: VRAM limits and long-form renders.
  • .claude/skills/video-prompt/SKILL.md: the agent skill, which is also a compact guide to writing H3 prompts.
  • examples/workflows/: the ComfyUI graphs the tiers produce.

Tests

python -m pytest

The tests need no GPU and no ComfyUI. The editor's JavaScript tests run from the same command and need Node 18 or newer on your PATH.

License

GPL-3.0, the same license as ComfyUI. See LICENSE. The bundled fonts are under the SIL Open Font License (js/standalone/screening-room/fonts/). Model weights are covered by their own licenses.
